Hyperpriors of spike-and-slab random effects

Source: R/randomEffects.R
betaPrior.Rd

Priors on the hyperparameters of spikeSlab(), in place of a given value or an estimate, for blocks with few groups, where an estimate of prob tends to 0 or 1 and an estimate of tau follows the modes.

  • betaPrior(a, b): prob ~ Beta(a, b), integrated out. The prior weight of a subset of k slab deviations among K is \(B(a + k, b + K - k) / B(a, b)\); betaPrior(1, 1) makes every number of slab deviations equally likely.

  • halfCauchyPrior(scale), halfNormalPrior(scale): on tau.

  • invGammaPrior(shape, rate): on tau^2.

em() estimates tau under a scale prior as the posterior mode, or with integrate = TRUE integrates the phase "exact" over log tau; see section Sparse random effects of em().

Usage

betaPrior(a = 1, b = 1)

halfCauchyPrior(scale = 1, integrate = FALSE)

halfNormalPrior(scale = 1, integrate = FALSE)

invGammaPrior(shape = 1, rate = 1, integrate = FALSE)

Arguments

a, b

Shape parameters of the Beta prior, positive.

scale

Scale of the half-Cauchy or half-normal prior, positive.

integrate

Logical. FALSE (default) takes the posterior mode of tau, TRUE integrates over log tau in the phase "exact".

shape, rate

Shape and rate of the inverse-gamma prior, positive.

Value

An object of class hyperprior.

See also

spikeSlab(), em()

Examples

spikeSlab(prob = betaPrior(1, 1), tau = halfCauchyPrior(1), mean = -1, spike = -Inf)
#> spikeSlab(prob = betaPrior(1, 1), tau = halfCauchyPrior(1), mean = -1, spike = -Inf)
